question: Does the NCBI Valencia search result support the claimed Barbodes tumba record in Valencia, Negros Oriental, and do the existing Negros accessions resolve the 2022 Malaunay River presentation?

boundedSearch.database: NCBI Nucleotide (nuccore), E-utilities ESearch and ESummary/EFetch

queries.interpretation: The unqualified place name Valencia combines distinct localities. Thirty-four records belong to the Pulangi River/Bukidnon sample set: 32 control-region records MG663358-MG663389 plus two COI records MG220325-MG220326. The other four are the separately labelled Negros Oriental COI records MT646827-MT646830.
No indexed Nucleotide record matched this text query. This is a bounded index-search outcome, not evidence that the fish is absent from Malaunay River.

limits: These are text-index searches; locality labels and taxon identifications are submitter supplied.
A zero-result query does not establish biological absence or prove that unpublished data do not exist.
No SRA, BioProject, BioSample, or sequence data were added to the app.

pulangiValenciaBukidnonCrossLocusRecords.assessment: Both COI records identify the Pulangi River site and have the same collection date, collectors, and voucher suffixes as two of the 32 Pulangi control-region records. They are strong same-sample cross-locus candidates, but a physical specimen or author-held voucher ledger was not checked; do not count the marker records as separate fish.
pulangiValenciaBukidnonCrossLocusRecords.coordinateCaveat: These are submitter archive coordinates for fish obtained through the study's fisher/vendor sampling. They are retained as source metadata and are not emitted as individual capture points or public map geometry.

negrosOrientalRangeExtensionLead.annualReport: The official Silliman University 2023 Annual Report says an undergraduate project titled DNA Barcoding of a Freshwater Barb, Barbodes tumba, in Valencia, Negros Oriental, Philippines was conducted June-August 2022.
negrosOrientalRangeExtensionLead.conferenceCitation: Christopher E. Bird's CV lists a 2022 NDiSTEM presentation titled New record of Barbodes tumba in Malaunay River, Negros Island using three mtDNA markers.

notPresentInInspectedRecords: project or poster identifier linking these records to the June-August 2022 project
the Cyt-b and 16S accessions implied by the conference title

negrosOrientalRangeExtensionLead.primaryMaterialSearch: The official Silliman annual report and TAMU-CC CV confirm project and presentation bibliographic details, but no poster, thesis text, specimen ledger, or three-marker accession crosswalk was located in this bounded search.
negrosOrientalRangeExtensionLead.assessment: The four MT646827-MT646830 records are distinct from the older Pulangi River records in Valencia City, Bukidnon. Their municipality-level Negros Oriental label does not identify Malaunay River. Their June 2020 submission predates the 2022 project described in the annual report, so the accession-to-project link remains unresolved; this chronology does not rule out unpublished or earlier preliminary sampling.
negrosOrientalRangeExtensionLead.waterbodyCrosswalk: The existing DENR-EMB Region VII table lead mentions Malaunay Spillway as a class boundary for Ocoy River, Sibulan; that water-quality classification wording does not establish that the presentation's Malaunay River is the same reach or provide fish occurrence geometry.

decision.taxonomy: No independent taxonomic re-identification performed; accession names remain submitter labels.
decision.historicalResearchEvidence: Retain the Mindanao Pulangi COI/D-loop marker links as probable same-sample archive crosswalks and retain the Negros Oriental accessions as a separate municipality-level molecular lead.
decision.visayasOccurrence: Not admitted. No retrieved primary record links a verified voucher, collection date, Malaunay River site, and the claimed three markers.

nextAction: National rollout step 396: move to the next waterbody-specific freshwater source review while keeping the Malaunay/Negros claim in the research-only access queue. Revisit it if an accessible primary poster, thesis, voucher ledger, or author-confirmed accession crosswalk appears.
